newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, bid-lists expected.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, bid-lists expected.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged in extremely quiet Monday action, as traders said a few bid-wanted lists were expected.
"There's absolutely nothing going on," one trader said of the muni secondary.
A second trader said the bid-wanted lists include several names that would help set the market's new levels, which are expected to be sharply lower than last week's.
The trader said he was watching Louisville and Jefferson Counties, Ky., sewer system bonds in particular. He said he expects the bonds to get bids at least 10 basis points off last week.
The market dropped sharply on Thursday, after a report on extremely strong home sales last month.
U.S. existing home sales surged nine percent to 4.26 million units, the second-highest rise on record. The figure exceeded the consensus estimate of 4.05 million units.
In economic news Monday, the U.S. Commerce Department said February personal income rose 0.9 percent, while spending increased 0.3 percent. The income increase was the largest since June 1996.
The government long bond also fell sharply last week, but was up 4/32 at 94-13/32 to yield 7.08 percent in early Monday action.
In the municipal secondary market, Alabama Housing Finance Authority 6.0s of 2021 were down 1/4 at 98-1/4.
Futures were higher, with the June municipal contract up 5/32 to 112-1/32 and June T-bonds 3/32 higher at 107-15/32. The MOB spread widened to 146 ticks from 144 at the close on Thursday.
This week's supply is even lower than last week's relatively small figure, at about $1.5 billion.
Negotiated offerings total $1.3 billion in 40 sales, with a $231 million Delaware County, Pa., Industrial Development Authority deal through Goldman, Sachs & Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 33 sales totaling $210 million are on the schedule, a $29 million Broome County, N.Y., deal is the largest.
